topic: Classifying Materials by Absorbency, Buoyancy, and Decay
key_concepts: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Matter exists as solid, liquid, and gas.
Solids can be classified by properties such as ability to absorb water.
Porous materials have small holes and absorb water; non-porous materials do not.
Cotton is a porous natural absorber of water.
Objects float when less dense than liquid and sink when denser.
Upthrust and buoyancy affect floating and sinking.
Some objects float initially then sink after absorbing water.
Decay breaks materials down through water, air, soil, and decomposers.
Biodegradable waste can be composted into fertilizer.
Non-biodegradable materials like plastics do not decompose easily.
Decomposers return organic waste to the ecosystem.
